title: Parametric model of the Milky Way for rendering
summary: Every number below is either a published measurement (with its reference key) or an explicit modelling choice (ref 'model'). Lengths in kpc unless a unit says otherwise. Angles in degrees. The model frame G is galactocentric (see frames.galactocentric).

units.extinction: mag of A_V per kpc of path

icrsToGalactic.note: IAU galactic coordinates as realised in the ICRS by the Hipparcos/Gaia convention: north galactic pole at (RA, Dec) = (192.85948, +27.12825) deg, galactic longitude of the north celestial pole = 122.93192 deg. Rows are the galactic x (l=0,b=0), y (l=90,b=0) and z (b=+90) axes written in ICRS components, so v_gal = M v_icrs. Differs from astropy's FK5-based Galactic frame by 0.02 arcsec (frame bias).

eclipticJ2000ToGalactic.note: v_gal = M v_ecl, where ecliptic J2000 uses the mean obliquity 84381.448 arcsec (the value the app and astronomy-engine use). M = icrsToGalactic x R_x(+eps). Treats EQJ as ICRS (the 23 mas frame bias is ignored).

appWorldToGalactic.note: The app's world axes are world = (x_ecl, z_ecl, -y_ecl). v_gal = M v_world. Its transpose maps galactic to world.

galactocentric.note: Model frame G (right-handed, kpc): origin at Sgr A*, x from the Sun's projection towards Sgr A*, y towards l = 90 deg (the direction of Galactic rotation at the Sun), z towards the north galactic pole; the Sun sits at z = +z0 above the midplane. Same construction as astropy's Galactocentric frame (roll = 0) with the parameters below. Transform from heliocentric galactic Cartesian (x_gal, kpc): x_G = R x_gal + sunG. Inverse: x_gal = R^T (x_G - sunG).
galactocentric.azimuthConvention: Galactocentric azimuth beta (as in Reid et al. 2019 and Chen et al. 2019): 0 towards the Sun, increasing in the direction of Galactic rotation. In frame G a point at radius R and azimuth beta is (x, y) = (-R cos beta, R sin beta).

peculiarVelocityUVW.note: Relative to the local standard of rest; U towards the Galactic centre, V towards rotation, W towards the NGP. Systematic uncertainties (1, 2, 0.5) km/s.

sgrAProperMotionAlongL.note: Apparent motion of Sgr A* along galactic longitude = reflex of the Sun's orbit. Total tangential speed of the Sun = 4.74047 x 6.411 x R0 = 251.5 km/s for R0 = 8.277 kpc.

thinDisc.density: rho = exp(-R/hR) * exp(-|z - zWarp(R,beta)|/hz), R <= Rmax

Rmax.note: Sampling limit only; BHG16 give no truncation radius. Density at 20 kpc is 1% of the local value.

thickDisc.density: rho = exp(-R/hR) * exp(-|z - zWarp|/hz), R <= Rmax

bulge.note: Box/peanut bulge. In-plane exponential along the bar's principal axes (WG13 fitted scale lengths); vertical exponential whose scale height varies along the major axis as measured by WG13, which produces the peanut shape seen side-on. The X-shape above ~400 pc is not modelled explicitly.
bulge.density: rho = exp(-sqrt((x/hx)^2 + (y/hy)^2)) * exp(-|z|/hz(|x|)); (x,y) along the bulge major/intermediate axes

barAngle.note: Angle between the major axis and the Sun-GC line; near end at positive longitude (first quadrant).

hzProfile.note: 0.18 kpc at x~0 (BHG16/WG13 minor-axis fit), 0.25/0.56/0.46 kpc at 0.525/1.125/1.725 kpc (WG13 conclusions). The 2.5 kpc node (0.20 kpc, the thin long bar's height from Wegg2015) is a model choice that joins the bulge to the long bar. Linear interpolation; constant beyond the ends.

stellarMass.note: Stellar mass in the VVV bulge region.

longBar.note: Two-component long bar of Wegg, Gerhard & Portail (2015) Table 1, 'N-body model + 2 components' row, fitted with R0 = 8.3 kpc. Cut(u) = exp(-u^2) if u > 1 else 1. For the super-thin component x0 < 0 means density rising outwards along x; we evaluate its in-plane term as |y|/y0 - |x|/|x0| (the cutoffs dominate; see galaxy.md).
longBar.density: rho = exp(-[(|x|/x0)^c + (|y|/y0)^c]^(1/c)) * exp(-|z|/z0) * Cut((R - Rout)/sOut) * Cut((Rin - R)/sIn)

nuclearStellarDisc.density: rho = (R/rb)^-1.3 for R < rb; (R/rb)^-3 for rb <= R < Redge; 0 beyond; times exp(-|z|/hz). Chosen so the projected profile along l goes as |l|^-0.3 inside ~90 pc and |l|^-2 outside, as BHG16 summarise.

Rmin.note: Inner sampling limit (avoids the integrable cusp).

nuclearStarCluster.density: Plummer sphere flattened to axis ratio q, half-light radius rh (Plummer scale a = rh / 1.305)

stellarHalo.density: rho = (m/rs)^-alphaIn for m < rs, (m/rs)^-alphaOut beyond, with m^2 = R^2 + (z/q(m))^2; q rises smoothly from qIn to qOut between 15 and 35 kpc (model)

alphaOut.note: RR Lyrae and BHB value; red giants give 3.8.

mRange.note: Sampling limits: inside 1 kpc the bulge dominates; 55 kpc keeps every particle inside the int16 position range.

spiralArms.note: Log-periodic spiral segments with one kink each: ln(R/Rkink) = -(beta - betaKink) tan(psi), psi = psiLt for beta <= betaKink, psiGt beyond. Gaussian 1-sigma width w(R) = width + 0.042 (R - Rkink) kpc. Reid et al. assumed R0 = 8.15 kpc; we scale every radius and width by R0/8.15 (= 1.0156) so the arms stay centred on Sgr A* and near-Sun distances change by < 2%. betaData is the azimuth range covered by parallaxes; outside it the arm is an extrapolation (see extension).

tangencyPriorsL.note: Bronfman et al. 2000 tangencies used by Reid et al. as priors in quadrant 4.

extension.note: Arms are continued beyond betaData with the pitch angle of the nearest segment for up to 90 deg of azimuth (30 deg for the short 3-kpc arm), inside 3.0 <= R <= 16.0 kpc (2.5 kpc for the 3-kpc arm). Along the extension the arm strength falls linearly from 0.6 at the data edge to 0 at the end. The far side of the Galaxy is not constrained by parallaxes.

youngArmStars.note: Young (<~100 Myr) OB-dominated population that makes the arms blue. Placed about the Reid et al. arm ridge lines with the fitted Gaussian widths; weight along each arm follows the thin-disc surface density times the arm length element.

hz.note: 'Young stars locally have a scale height of ~60 pc' (Wegg et al. 2015, sec. 7, citing Joshi 2007).

hiiRegions.note: Individual HII regions drawn as compact pink sprites along the arms. Positions are a model (sampled like the young stars); scale height from the maser-traced high-mass star-forming regions.

hz.note: Scale height of high-mass star-forming regions within 7 kpc of the centre.

lineRatios.note: Hbeta/Halpha = 1/2.86 is Case B recombination at 10^4 K (Osterbrock & Ferland 2006); the metal-line ratios are typical of Galactic HII regions and only set the display colour.

warp.density: zWarp(R, beta) = a (R - Rw)^b sin(beta - betaW) for R > Rw, else 0
warp.note: Power-law fit to 1339 classical Cepheids ('All' row), fitted with R0 = 8.0 kpc; Rw scaled by R0/8.0 here. Applied to all disc components, arms and dust.

dust.note: Dust density expressed directly as V-band extinction per unit path, a_V = 1.086 kappaV rho, where rho is Drimmel & Spergel's dust density (MJy/sr/kpc) and kappaV their fitted V opacity. D&S defined the model with R_sun = 1 (8 kpc); we evaluate their formulas at x/s with s = R0/8.0 and divide the density by s, which keeps every column density they fitted unchanged. The arm dust uses D&S's cross-section, height and radial cut-off but is placed on the Reid et al. 2019 arm ridge lines (D&S used the Taylor & Cordes 1993 arms). D&S's separate Local-arm dust segment and the Sag-Car reduction factor are not used. No central molecular zone.

disc.density: rho0 exp(-r/hr) sech^2(z/hd(r)); hd = hd0 + hd1 (r - rf) for r > rf; for r < rHole: rho(rHole) exp(-((r - rHole)/sHole)^2)

arms.density: rhoA gA(Ra) exp(-(d/wa)^2) exp(-(z/ha)^2); wa = ca Ra; ha = ha0 + ha1 (Ra - rfa)^2 for Ra > rfa; gA = exp(-((Ra - rm)/ra)^2) for Ra > rm, else 1. d = in-plane distance to the arm ridge, Ra = galactocentric radius of the nearest ridge point.

checks.note: Values computed from this model by staging/galaxy/src/galaxyModel.ts (see galaxy.md): a_V in the plane at the Sun, and A_V from the Sun to Sgr A* and to the galactic poles, against the literature.

luminosity.note: V-band luminosity budget used to set particle brightness. Total from the Milky Way analogue photometry of Licquia et al. 2015 (M_V = -21.37, B-V = 0.73) as tabulated by BHG16, with M_V,sun = 4.83. The split between components is a model: stellar masses from the references above divided by assumed mass-to-light ratios (thick disc 3.4, bulge 3.2, thin bar 3.0, super-thin bar 1.5, NSD 3.0, halo 1.5; M/L_V of old populations with a Kroupa IMF lie between ~1.5 and ~4), with the remainder given to the thin disc. The implied thin-disc M/L_V is 1.8, compared with 1.70 for the Galaxy as a whole (BHG16 Table 3).

colours.note: Display colours. Each particle gets a B-V drawn from a normal distribution, converted to an effective temperature with Ballesteros (2012) and to linear sRGB through a blackbody and the CIE 1931 fit of Wyman, Sloan & Shirley (2013), the same pipeline the app uses for stars. Integrated population colours are not blackbodies; this is a display approximation. HII regions use the emission-line mix in components.hiiRegions.lineRatios.
